about.title: Pomona Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: When you sit in an exam room or a hospital bed in Pomona, you are trusting someone else's training. Sometimes that trust is broken, and a missed diagnosis, a medication mix-up, or a surgical error leaves you worse off than when you walked in. Pomona is a city of roughly 153,000 people in eastern Los Angeles County, and in 2025 alone 1,428 residents and visitors were injured in traffic collisions here, a reminder of how often people rely on local emergency care. California treats medical negligence differently from an ordinary injury claim. Under MICRA you generally have one year from when you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to file. A 90-day notice must go to the provider first, and a qualified medical expert nearly always has to explain how the standard of care was breached. We handle medical malpractice claims in Pomona on a contingency basis, so you owe nothing in fees unless there is a recovery.

items.title: The MICRA clock is shorter than most people expect
items.desc: California generally allows one year from the date you discovered the harm, and no more than three years from the injury, to bring a medical negligence claim. Getting in touch early keeps those options open.

items.title: The 90-day notice and expert review are handled for you
items.desc: Before suit can be filed, a 90-day notice must go to the provider, and a qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in. Our team takes on both steps.

items.title: Honest talk about the non-economic damages cap
items.desc: California caps non-economic damages in malpractice cases, and that cap rises every year. We can explain what the current figure means for a claim like yours, without inflating expectations.

items.question: I was treated after a crash on I-10 in Pomona and something went wrong at the hospital. Is that a malpractice case or part of the accident claim?
items.answer: It can be both, and they are handled differently. The driver who hit you may be responsible for the crash injuries, while a provider whose care fell below the accepted standard may be separately responsible for the added harm. We can sort out which claim covers what, since the MICRA deadlines and notice rules apply only to the medical side.

items.question: My surgery didn't go the way the doctor said it would. Does that mean I have a case?
items.answer: Not by itself. California law is clear that a bad outcome alone is not malpractice; there has to be a departure from the standard of care that caused your harm. That is why a qualified medical expert is almost always needed to review the records. Talking it through with us costs nothing and helps you understand whether a review makes sense.

items.question: How much does it cost to have a Pomona malpractice attorney look at my records?
items.answer: Nothing up front. We work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Keep in mind that expert review is a normal part of these cases, and we will explain how those costs are handled before anything moves forward.
